body.statement: The Ejaz--Bareinboim \(\rho\)-Markovian restriction in Definition 3.2 requires that no ground endogenous variable have an exogenous relational parent and permits a non-relational exogenous parent to be shared only by attributes of the same instance.  Separately, Section 5 assumptions (I)--(III) specify the neural-completeness domain, including finite observed domains and one uniform finite bound on relational-parent multiset size over every admissible skeleton in the declared domain.  Theorem 5.2 establishes RNCM expressivity, while Algorithm 1 together with Appendix D, Corollary D.7 in arXiv v2 supplies sound and complete neural identification on that Section 5 domain.
body.justification: The comparator qualification requires the published Definition 3.2 restrictions to be separated from the Section 5 neural-completeness domain and its result attribution.
body.gap: This dependency-free cited substrate is not a contribution of the present note.

source.verbatim_statement: [Definition 3.2] We say an RSCM M is ρ-Markovian if for each variable O.A in V, the set of exogenous relational parents is empty. We say M is Markovian if it is ρ-Markovian and no two variables O.A,T.B in V share a non-relational exogenous parent. [D.3 assumptions] (I) M is ρ-Markovian. (II) All variables in V have discrete, finite domains. (III) There is a non-negative integer D such that for any skeleton ρ, the grounding Mρ has variables o.A with relational parent multisets of size at most D. [Theorem 5.2] For every RSCM M over S inducing relational causal graph G, there exists a G-RNCM N such that for every skeleton ρ, the ground RSCMs Mρ and Nρ induce the same counterfactual distributions over Vρ. [Algorithm 1 and Corollary D.7] As a corollary of Thm. 5.2, we can derive that Alg. 1 is sound and complete for the task of relational identification. Then, Q is not FAIL if and only if the query is relationally identifiable dependent on the data from G and P, in which case Q equals the query.
